title: Independent film makers: how did you make it happen?

commenti.body:
Well.. what do you need more? Why do you need  big funding? Seriously, with how affordable everything is nowadays. Get a camera, some aputure lights, learn the craft. What actually do you need more?

Not to be harsh or something, but funding will not be the deciding factor in your success. And is certainly not something to hold you back. Skills and experience will make the difference. We have all the tools available. Equipment that film makers 60 years could not have dreamt of (and even affordable too). And yet there seem the to be less driven filmmakers than back then. 

Besides that your trailer actually portrays a high quality looking production. It only doesn’t convince you to watch it. So start there, before you blame the lack of funding.

>We have all the tools available. Equipment that film makers 60 years could not have dreamt of (and even affordable too).

This is a great point. It's easier to make a movie now than ever before.

There is funding available.

Do you know how much money is floating around out in the world? There are literally billionaires in support groups trying to figure out how to spend their money.

Filmmakers decide instead to go after the most predictable routes competing with each other.

If you have a killer idea, create a killer package, leverage your network and go out and pitch to ultra wealthy people for the amount of money that you need. Period.
How sure are you that there are less motivated filmmakers than back than? Cause if that is really true it will give me a lot of hope in my future carreer

A huge generalization of course. But if you look what independent film makers did in the 70s with the limits they had. If you look at directors like Sam Raimi or Coen Brothers first movies. Or William Friedkin literally risking his life during the car chase in French Connection. The will they had is insane.

You're right, this generation don't have a clue. They are culturally unaware, perpetually bored by modern life's abundances and unable to create any art at all which isn't riddled with pastiche, trite literary devices or "underlying themes". The pure aesthetic no longer exists because there is no place for it anymore. This has been substituted with pretentious and pseudo-deep commentary, bathetic quips, and "clever" plot twists. I was in film school with a bunch of kids who wanted to direct Marvel movies and thought Fight Club was *literally* the best thing ever. It's a fucking travesty.

Do you genuinely believe it's that easy? 

The hardest part of this comment is "leverage your network"

As in everything it's all about who you know, and who knows and likes you. If you know someone who can get you into the right doors you can do anything, even if you suck at what you want to do (just look at how many nepotism recipients make terrible projects in Hollywood)

If you DONT know those people....good luck. Try really hard and you might meet the right people who give a crap. But don't pretend it's easy, especially when most people are poor as hell and have to spend much of their time earning their daily bread

Everyone is shrugging off funding like it’s not important. Even if you’re not paying your crew regular rates, you still have to feed them. You can leverage and ask for favors when you’re doing shorts, but if you’re shooting a feature, don’t expect anyone to work for free. Don’t forget transportation. But again, feed your cast and crew! Film schools should have a mandatory class for catering.

So let’s jump ahead and now you’re miraculously done with your feature and want to get it out independently. You can either post it online and get no traction, or you can bring it to the festival circuit. Okay, that’s at least another few grand at a minimum for submission fees. If you want an actual film career, you have to actually spend money to go to the festivals. $$$

None of that had anything to do with the actual filmmaking itself, but that’s already at least $10k you should be okay spending before you think about which camera you want to use, limitations you’d have to put on yourself for props/locations/actors, keeping the schedule as short as possible, etc.

Filmmaking is fucking expensive, even if it’s a single location drama.
Yeah, the local film making club here is people trying to make big budget action on a 500 dollar budget and every film has to have that end point plot reversal.

Uhm.

We got the money for funding by mostly funding ourselves and then doing a kickstarter. We made a low budget indie doc in less than ten years, which is what most zero fund docs take to make. We did it in 6 and a half.

You can go see sections of it. It meets fairly high standards of quality. 

What have you done that made any money?

What do you think worked for your production?

Lots of good cheap gear. But moving and feeding a crew, especially for a doc costs money.

Even my little BMPCC is ten times better than what I had 40 years ago.

just reread and noticed your comment about the trailer not making people want to watch it.

Well, that is pretty lame criticism. Like the worst kind of it actually.

If you think it is not a good trailer, then tell me what it needs to improve.

I am not proud at all on my trailer if it can be better, so tell me how to make it better.

Because as a 60 year old unknown film maker I just happen to hang out with all these ultra rich people and they just write me checks.

LOL I got a stack of scripts I can't afford to make.
Check ur dm! My comment was pretty long already so thats why i didnt elaborate.

Yeah, you can feed the crew ramen right? 

ha ha ha 

We had to move a small crew all over the country. We shot in about 10 different cities. The film took 6 and a half years to make. It was a two man crew as everything including archiving thousands of artifacts because we had no money for an archivist.

A large expense was getting a professional score.

On a previous film we tried the fest thing. Learned a lot. Your indie is going to end up in a minor B class fest. As you say, you will spend a fortune on festival entrance fees. the result of all that will be minimal.

We thought we would try something else. Our film is about gaming so it gets shown for free at game conventions as one way to develop traction. half is free on YT.

We're making a ton more cash publishing game material now than we ever have made with the film.

We are even operating an annual game convention now.

Amazing that people downvote my comment. There is money everywhere.

Learn to NETWORK. Decide what you want, believe in it, and the kick the doors down until you get there. If you want to be meek and passive while preaching "it's tough out there!" you have chosen the wrong industry.

Didn't say it's easy, but I genuinely KNOW that a path exists to whatever you want, and however much you want.

Don't worry, most people think like you do so you'll find plenty of groups and echo chambers to reinforce your limiting beliefs.

I am the crazy one.

Trust me, I know how to network.

See, I made this 2 hour documentary.

I am just curious how other film makers managed their productions from funding to marketing and distribution.

The real issue is getting your film seen.

Sort of amusing that everyone reads the first pargraph where I talk about how it is hard to fund a film and ignores the rest.

If you go to the link provided you will see I have made a film already. 

Making the film consumed my life for 6 and a half years.

I was merely asking how other film makers managed the various stages of making and selling.

I mentioned money first because that is the reality of most indie films. If you want to make your film you are most likely going to have to fund it yourself.

Maybe I should have been clearer. I do not need advice on how to fund a film because I did it out of pocket and when we had drafts, the first was 6 hours long, we turned to kickstarter.

[https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/secretsofblackmoor/secrets-of-blackmoor-the-true-history-of-dungeons](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/secretsofblackmoor/secrets-of-blackmoor-the-true-history-of-dungeons)

Sure, I'd be curious to find out how you funded your film, yet, most responses seem to be from people who may not have actually ever made a feature length film. Telling someone, "dude, you gotta talk to people" is not exactly a case study from another film maker.

I am not complaining either as now I seem to have changed careers from film maker to game publisher and that's much more lucrative than indie film making. 

And, I hope this does not come off as snotty and mean or angry. I am actually quite cherry and fun most of the time.

LOL that's all fine and dandy.

I have a finished film.

You can even rent it on Amazon.

https://www.amazon.com/Secrets-Blackmoor-History-Dungeons-Dragons/dp/B087QN51WF/ref=sr\_1\_1?crid=DCNCRN9URAH2&keywords=secrets+of+blackmoor&qid=1707152676&sprefix=secrets+of+blackmoor%2Caps%2C142&sr=8-1

You need to write the screenplay and the film around your budget.  You can do a lot of cool and original things without grand set designs. of course you cant really do a period piece with grand scope and scale.
Yeah, it does really begin with the writing that's for sure.
